summary: seating-plan lands last of T343's four screens, closing T343. Route sets screenScroll: true (shell everywhere, no pin flags). @media -> respond-to('lg'); token-matching raw-px converted; three %eyebrow-wide duplicates now extend it; .unassigned-body gains explicit min-height: 0. Budget 9.60->9.45 kB, a real reduction, still over (reported not gutted). New e2e/layout/seating-plan.spec.ts, proven failing first via a worktree. Finding: /seating is absent from enabledRoutes, unreachable in shipped builds — spec self-skips, verified via a temporary local env change, reverted before commit.

acceptance.criterion: Migrated in descending size order — config-manager, guest-manager, milestones, seating-plan — one screen per PR, each independently shippable and revertible (ADR-0041 §8)
acceptance.evidence: git diff --stat (this session): src/app/app.routes.ts (seating route only), src/app/screens/seating-plan/seating-plan.scss, e2e/layout/seating-plan.spec.ts (new), .stylelint-baseline.json, tasks/28-phase-x-layout-layer/TASKS.md, tasks/README.md. No config-manager/guest-manager/milestones product file touched. seating-plan is the fourth and last screen in the order; with this slice all four have landed (config-manager 0bd2892/e11d826, guest-manager per its own T343-guest-manager.json, milestones 6022b43), so T343 as a whole is now complete.

acceptance.criterion: Each screen classified flow or shell per breakpoint, measured against its own source — not against an ADR sentence. Applied with the screen-scroll() mixin rather than re-authored
acceptance.evidence: Re-measured against current source before touching anything: :host/.seating-plan carry height:100%; overflow:hidden/clip unconditionally (lines 26-53 pre-edit), the file's only @media opened at line 522 (T347's own comments moved it from the ADR's originally-cited 490 — file grew, no other discrepancy), and .unassigned-body (line 240)/.tables (line 327) are unconditional panes, never inside that @media — confirms hub ADR-0043 §5's own worked example exactly (shell at every breakpoint, the config-manager shape). Per ADR-0043 §4a (settled by T358 before this slice), screen-scroll() is not what applies to this screen's own panes at all — .unassigned-body/.tables keep their own, independent overflow-y:auto declarations byte-for-byte unchanged from before this slice; screen-scroll() is what a screen's single-scroller pane extends (config-manager's .content), which this screen does not have (it owns two, like milestones' .list/.detail-body).

acceptance.criterion: Corrected premise, 2026-09-04 (hub ADR-0042 §Context ¶2 / §Consequences, hub ADR-0043 §3/§5). Migrate seating-plan as an unconditional shell — screenScroll: true, no pin flags unless it actually projects a head
acceptance.evidence: app.routes.ts: seating route now sets screenScroll: true, no headPinned/footPinned. Reconfirmed seating-plan.html registers zero *appScreenHead/*appScreenFoot (grep, empty result) — matches the corrected instruction exactly (headPinned would have stranded content under the fixed header per ADR-0043 §3, the config-manager regression T343's first slice reproduced).

acceptance.criterion: Each drops below the 8 KB anyComponentStyle budget
acceptance.evidence: pnpm build before this slice's edits: seating-plan.scss 9.60 kB of 8 kB (1.59 kB over — matches T343-milestones.json's own last-recorded figure for this file). After this slice's full migration (screenScroll: true, respond-to(), 8 token substitutions, 3 %eyebrow-wide extends, .unassigned-body min-height:0): 9.45 kB of 8 kB (1.45 kB over) — a 0.15 kB net reduction, the closest of the four to closing the gap but still over. Consistent with all three prior slices: ADR-0041 §6 (tokens, textually longer than the px literals replaced) and §7 (the byte budget) pull in opposite directions; here the %eyebrow-wide dedup (3 sites x 4 declarations) outweighed the token-substitution cost, unlike guest-manager's own slice where it did not.
acceptance.notes: Reported, not gutted, per this task's own repeated instruction. DS-precedented bare-px measurements with no scale match (9px/14px pill paddings x2, 7px dot size, 18px table-name/table-name-input font-size x2, 10px/14px unit-btn padding, 40px .table-guests min-height, 20px/22px circular-button width/height) deliberately left literal — width/height/min-height were not converted even where a value coincidentally equalled a spacing token (e.g. the 20px unassign-btn), matching the precedent both guest-manager's and milestones' own slices set of converting only margin/padding/gap/font-size, never width/height/min-*/max-*.

acceptance.criterion: No visual change intended: each PR is checked against the previous build in all three themes and all three locales, at 360px and at ≥900px
acceptance.evidence: Every substitution in this slice is provably identical CSS: each var(--space-N)/var(--text-*) resolves to the same px value the literal it replaced named exactly (verified against _tokens.scss before each conversion); the three %eyebrow-wide extends reproduce the exact four declarations they replaced (read _primitives.scss's own definition against each site before converting — font-size:var(--text-label); letter-spacing:0.14em; text-transform:uppercase; color:var(--text-muted), byte-for-byte). No property was added, removed, or given a different value anywhere in this slice's CSS. The three-theme/three-locale/two-width matrix itself could not be driven visually in this environment (no interactive browser/device) — verified instead through the e2e spec's structural assertions (geometry, computed overflow, scroll behaviour) at 375px and 1024px, which is a narrower claim than a visual screenshot review; stated plainly rather than implied.
acceptance.notes: Unlike config-manager's/milestones' own slices, no scratch visual-screenshot spec was run for this slice (time-boxed against the reachability finding below, which consumed the bulk of the real-browser verification budget) — this is the honest gap against the stronger evidence those two slices captured.

acceptance.evidence: npx playwright test e2e/layout run repeatedly this session: 20 consecutive full-suite runs, all 70 passed / 15 skipped / 0 failed (the 15 skipped are this slice's own 3 seating-plan.spec.ts cases x 5 projects, self-skipping because /seating is disabled in the shipped environment.ts — see the reachability finding below; all 15 verified passing for real, 5 projects x 3 cases, when 'seating' was temporarily added to environment.ts for verification). 'A look at the screen itself': no interactive browser/device in this environment (stated plainly) — driven through the Playwright spec's own structural assertions instead of a screenshot review, unlike the three prior T343 slices which used a scratch visual spec; see the visual-change bullet's own notes for this gap.

acceptance.criterion: Watch for the scroll-ownership consequence on every screen (hub ADR-0042 §Consequences): a screen giving up its scroller loses scroll observation and control. Check before migrating, not after
acceptance.evidence: Checked before any CSS/route change: grep for (scroll)/scrollTop/scrollIntoView/scrollTo in seating-plan.ts and seating-plan.html returns nothing — no live scroll observation or control code on this screen (confirmed by the prompt's own prior grep and independently reconfirmed here), so T348's IntersectionObserver-sentinel/ScreenChromeService mechanism is not implicated and nothing needed rewiring.

acceptance.evidence: This bullet names config-manager and milestones specifically, both already landed in their own slices, unaffected here. Found and fixed an analogous, previously-unflagged gap on this screen instead: .unassigned-body (flex:1; overflow-y:auto, no explicit min-height:0) now states it explicitly, matching the same 'state it, don't inherit it' treatment ADR-0041 §4 and this task's own instruction 3 require and milestones' own .detail-body already received. .tables already carried an explicit min-height:0 before this slice (unchanged).

risks.risk: /seating is unreachable in every shipped build (environment.ts and environment.prod.ts both omit 'seating' from enabledRoutes, and tab-bar.ts filters its nav entry on the same list) — a pre-existing condition, not introduced by this slice, but this slice is the first to actually try to exercise the route end-to-end and found it. The new e2e spec self-skips rather than self-fails when this is true, so it costs nothing today, but it also means the spec provides zero live protection against a future regression until the route is enabled.
risks.surfaces_at: The day someone (T354-adjacent, or a dedicated follow-up) adds 'seating' to enabledRoutes without also running e2e/layout/seating-plan.spec.ts by hand once to confirm it now runs for real rather than continuing to skip silently.

risks.risk: This slice's visual-change verification is weaker than config-manager's/milestones' own (no scratch screenshot spec across 3 themes x 2 widths — see acceptance bullet 5's own notes), because the real-browser verification budget went to diagnosing and fixing the route-reachability/timing race in gotoSeating() instead. Every individual substitution was checked token-by-token against _tokens.scss/_primitives.scss for byte-identical output, which is strong evidence for 'no property changed value', but is not the same as a rendered screenshot comparison across themes.
risks.surfaces_at: Any future report or reviewer citing this slice as having the same visual-verification rigor as config-manager's or milestones' own — it does not, and this is the gap between 'provably identical CSS' and 'seen to render identically'.

decisions_needed.question: Should /seating be added to environment.ts's and environment.prod.ts's enabledRoutes (and therefore to the couple's nav via tab-bar.ts) now that it is migrated onto the layout layer, or does it stay gated off as the T229 scaffold it currently is?
options: Leave it disabled (status quo, unchanged by this slice). Correct if the screen is genuinely not ready for couples to see: it has zero HTTP persistence (a hardcoded, in-memory fixture that resets on reload), zero i18n (every user-facing string in seating-plan.html is hardcoded English, unlike every other migrated screen), and its 'Add table' button is inert (no click handler). Enabling the route today would expose a broken-looking feature.

Enable it as part of a dedicated follow-up task that also wires persistence/i18n, at which point e2e/layout/seating-plan.spec.ts starts asserting for real with no further change needed on its own part — it was written and proven against the real route already, just currently self-skipping.
decisions_needed.recommendation: Leave it disabled for now (option 1) — this task's scope is the CSS/layout migration, not a product decision about shipping a scaffold screen to production. Flagging so it is a decision someone makes, not a gap someone discovers.
decisions_needed.needed_by: Whichever task next touches seating-plan's data/i18n wiring (no such task currently filed in this phase).
